Major Takeaways In this final section, we will present major takeaways from the residential building stock characterization of PBC, the major takeaways from the electricity, utility bill, and emissions savings as a result of upgrade packages presented for low-income households in PBC and next steps that PBC representatives could consider utilizing this information and gather more pertinent data to improve the energy performance of the existing residential buildings in the county. For the residential building stock characterization, we identified three major takeaways. The first major takeaway is that 60% of housing units in PBC are single-family dwellings and approximately 70% of these dwellings are occupied by the owner. Second, a majority of multi-family housing units are in buildings with less than 30 units and approximately 60% of these dwellings are occupied by renters. Third, over 90% of HVAC systems in PBC are individual systems. The high prevalence of these systems may be beneficial to program design based on the fact that repetition factors and economies of scale can be achieved. Similarly for the modeled electricity, utility bill, and emissions impact for low-income households in PBC based with the various upgrade packages, we identified three major takeaways. The first major takeaway is that ENERGY STAR and Ultra-high Efficiency Heat Pump decrease annual electricity consumption by 6% and 20%, respectively. Based on FPL electricity rates, this equates to a modeled decrease of annual utility bills by ~$150 and nearly $500, respectively. Second, the full electrification with high-efficiency appliances decreases modeled annual electricity consumption by an additional 9% or approximately $200 in annual utility bill savings.
